name: Kwoma-Manambu Pidgin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record kwom1264 and reference record 310382 (MED = Bowden 1997, 'wordlist_or_less', 3 pp.; the only reference attached to the languoid).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; confirms Bowden 1997:337-339 is the sole documentation.

sources.citation: Bowden, Ross. 1997. A Dictionary of Kwoma: a Papuan language of north-east New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-134. Canberra: ANU. Appendix B 'Kwoma-Manambu lingua franca used in inter-ethnic trading', pp. 337-339 (DOI 10.15144/PL-C134, ANU open repository).
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix B is a 14-phrase sample text (Councillor Paul Martin, Bangwis, Jan 1994) with word-by-word Kwoma/Manambu source tags, free English and Tok Pisin translations and a Kwoma equivalent; no phonological or prosodic remarks of any kind. The dictionary's own orthography/pronunciation notes (pp. xxix-xxx) concern Kwoma proper and are also silent on stress.

sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 2008. The Manambu Language of East Sepik, Papua New Guinea. Oxford: Oxford University Press (chapter on language contact / multilingualism, where the Kwoma-Manambu lingua franca is mentioned citing Bowden 1997:337-8).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; Harvard e-access not checked
sources.note: Only other scholarly work known to mention the pidgin; worth checking whether Aikhenvald adds any first-hand observation (e.g. that Manambu speakers pronounce the mixed code with Manambu accentuation) beyond the Bowden citation. Also the primary description of Manambu stress, one of the two component languages.

sources.citation: Bowden, Ross. Field recordings / notes, Bangwis village 1994 (text dictated by Councillor Paul Martin) -- if archived (e.g. PARADISEC or La Trobe/Monash anthropology archives).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: An audio recording of the Appendix B text would be the only conceivable basis for any prosodic statement about this pidgin; no published phonology exists.
